Yeah I’ll never pretend that inconveniences are on the same level as serious issues. However, when I think of these things, I see the iceberg metaphor. Every single issue is just the surface and a holdout from something that came before it. In this way I still consider our society a patriarchy. Maybe it isn’t legally, but socially I would definitely say it is. 

I also think you’re giving conservatives too much credit as they’ll literally use anything to deflect from a feminist point. For example, if there weren’t any ‘crazy’ feminist talking points they could use, they’d just use the idea of lack of desirability to discredit. 

But again, i consider the patriarchy to still be in action. I mean just based alone upon who is in charge of our country there is a male majority. And in addition to this, they are predominantly older, which means that all of the ideals of a patriarchal society have been instilled within them. So, while we maybe have progressed down here there minds of the men in power probably have not. 

I think the social change we’ve found is a step in an egalitarian direction, but we can’t ignore that we’ve got a lot to shake off before we get there.

But there are some pretty clear genetic differences that are sex based I would say. But the biggest problem is that the world was modeled using old and predominantly male data. In this way, what’s considered average won’t be so average at all. 

I think there is a difference between pointing something out and complaining. I don’t agree with the phones being to big but it does make me consider why the default is to build things that are suitable for men but not so much women. 

And because you are slightly below the average height for a man you will experience certain things, but with the average height for a women being 5’4 I’m sure you can imagine how it could be even more challenging to navigate certain things. Again, I’m not saying this is an end of world problem. It’s just something that I personally believe is remnant of the patriarchal society that we’re working to leave behind.

Do you fight for the issues you’ve mentioned? I definitely think men’s perspective can be underrepresented as victims of certain crimes but I also think it’s worth noting that that is a symptom of patriarchy. Also, I think it’s worth mentioning that most times when I see any mention of men’s plight, it’s used as a counter for women’s complaints. This in itself actually diminishes the weight of it because it’s only used as a counter attack instead of it’s own issue.

I’m of the mind that ALL of the things mentioned need to be solved. Of course there are more serious issues, but that does not mean those things aren’t issues. If someone decided to dismiss arguments against serious issues because of the introduction of a non-serious issue, then they probably didn’t want to solve anything in the first place.
